key_insight: The paper turns one-step generative surrogate modeling for stochastic dynamics into a joint-drift problem, using a block-triangular structure so the current state is preserved while the next state can be sampled conditionally in one model call.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast stochastic trajectory generation with one evaluation per time step, making it attractive for computational science workflows that need accurate uncertainty propagation at lower cost.
method: Apply drifting to the empirical joint distribution of consecutive states instead of requiring multiple next-state samples per current state.
Use a block-triangular projected drift field that keeps the current-state marginal unchanged.
Make the second block act as a direct sampler of the conditional distribution of the next state.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing accurate marginal and trajectory-dependent statistics, with favorable accuracy-cost tradeoffs versus deterministic, diffusion-, flow-, and distillation-based surrogates.
watch_item: The approach relies on having representative trajectory pairs and on the projection/drift architecture being well-conditioned; performance may degrade if the observed joint data are sparse or poorly cover rare transitions.
paper_title: One-Step Generative Surrogate Models via Block-Triangular Joint Drifting
